children.name: Dactylocalyx pumiceus Stutchbury, 1841
children.description: Basiphytous, cup- to barrel or vase-shaped, plate-like or calyciform sponge measuring 22 – 53 cm long by 17 – 30 cm wide and 23 mm thick (Fig. 6 A – F). Surface microhispid, irregular, grooved in both internal and external sides and perforated by small caliber tubules (Fig. 6 G). Grooves up to 3 – 30 mm wide and 8 – 50 mm deep (Fig. 6 F, H). Color in vivo white, cream or greenish-yellow, becoming white or cream in ethanol. Consistency firm but friable. Skeleton (Fig. 7): Dictyonal skeleton thick, stout to thin and fragile, tuberculated, forming polygonal meshes (mainly triangular and quadrangular with rounded corners), and with connections tip-to-tip and tip-to-node (Fig. 7 A – D). Network of small tubules dense, ramified, irregularly anastomosed. Siliceous prominences project through the surface (Fig. 7 A). Dermalia with fused hexactins, diactins and discohexasters. Atrialia with spined hexactins and pentactins, free or fused to the dictyonalia, diactins, and free hexasters in variable abundance (Fig. 7 D). Spicules: Megascleres are fused hexactins and free large diactins, asymmetrical pentactins and hexactins. Microscleres are discohexasters, onychohexasteres and rare oxyhexasters (Figs 7 E – F, 8, 9; Table 2). Fused hexactins irregular, asymmetrical, with straight, microspined actins 55 – 96 µm long by 7 – 10 µm thick, club-shaped, with expanded, rounded endings (Fig. 7 E – F). Large diactins smooth, crossing transversally the skeleton, always broken (not shown).
